tweets: A Hoysala king broke ground on this temple in 1117 CE. It took 103 years and three kings' reigns to finish. 🛕
Vishnuvardhana commissioned the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur, Karnataka, dedicating it to Vishnu as Chennakeshava — the handsome Keshava. His successors kept building long after he was gone.

Entire walls are carved from soapstone, soft enough to chisel fine detail when freshly quarried, hardening with age. The result: thousands of sculpted figures, friezes of elephants, dancers, and epic scenes wrapping the temple's base.
Look up and you'll find 48 lathe-turned pillars, no two alike. One, the Narasimha pillar, could once be spun by hand on its base — stone engineering centuries ahead of its time.

Started by a king, finished by his grandson over a century later, and in 2023 inscribed by UNESCO as part of the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas. Some things are worth taking 103 years to get right. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
